rating.reasoning_summary: This strand tracks the memetic evolution of 'writing manifestos' as a coordination technology, anchored by @exgenesis's 2024 manifesto on 'refactoring multiscale human coordination by naturalizing woo.' The arc moves from casual social prompts (2020: 'everyone should write a manifesto') through @exgenesis's concrete implementation (April 2024), to meta-discussions about manifestos-as-infrastructure (August 2024: forking/clustering manifestos via LLMs). The boundary object is the manifesto itself as a genre for articulating individual agency within collective coordination problems. However, the strand lacks execution beyond the initial artifact—no evidence of the '5-year plan' materializing, no follow-up coordination infrastructure, and minimal uptake of the 'woo naturalization' frame outside endorsements. It's aspirational philosophy with high scene resonance but low real-world traction.

essential_tweets.annotation: 2020 origin: The casual prompt 'everyone should write a manifesto' as social game, pre-dating serious coordination framing
April 2024: @exgenesis's pre-manifesto thread articulating the core problem ('refactor multiscale coordination via woo')
The Artifact: Launch of the manifesto itself, establishing 'naturalizing woo' as the boundary object
Validation from @RichDecibels highlighting the 'ontological gap' between rationalism and wisdom traditions

@Malcolm_Ocean proposing 'bespoke memetic payloads' to avoid politicization—tactical evolution of dissemination strategy

title: Can a manifesto make woo… operational?
summary:
The hottest line in this whole saga is @exgenesis basically pitching a five‑year speedrun: “refactor multiscale human coordination by making woo compatible with modern ontologies and injecting it into society.” It’s not framed like a self-help doc—it’s framed like a coordination hack: take wisdom traditions that don’t translate inside rationalist/scientific language, build the “ontological critical path,” and ship it as something society can actually use.

The arc starts as a casual social game (@mechanical_monk in 2020: “every one of my mutuals should write a manifesto”), then hard-swerves into earnest ambition in April 2024 when @exgenesis posts the pre-manifesto “should I start an institute?” thread and immediately hits the wall: what’s the concrete deliverable of a “coordination refactor”? The manifesto drop (Apr 25) becomes the boundary object everyone can point to. @RichDecibels quotes the most poetic bit about the “tension” between scientific rational frameworks and wisdom traditions that “can’t travel across the gap,” while @TylerAlterman plays the adult in the room: not all woo can be naturalized, but there’s “enormous alpha” in forcing woo and science into conversation (which @exgenesis tightens to “the parts… that can be”). Meanwhile @Malcolm_Ocean pushes it from philosophy to distribution strategy: make “bespoke memetic payloads” for different tribes (left/right) so the core idea doesn’t get instantly politicized.

Then the energy peaks and diffuses into meta-infrastructure fantasies: @DefenderOfBasic (Aug 2024) proposes a “manifesto game jam” + LLM semantic clustering + GitHub forking—"The Manifesto Web"—so manifestos become matchmaking/coordination rails, not just declarations. After that, it kind of… doesn’t land anywhere concrete: lots of praise, some tactical refinement, but no visible institute or five-year execution pipeline. Still, it matters if you care about the perennial problem: everyone agrees “coordination is the bottleneck” (see @danallison’s later viral thread vibe), but the moment coordination starts feeling mystical/spooky, rationalists flinch—this thread is one of the cleaner attempts to build a translation layer instead of picking a side.
